answer: Make reputation decay. Every account's voting weight loses 10% each epoch and is restored only by fresh, peer-attested work, capped at 1 point earned per epoch. A dormant farm of 1,000 puppets bought once fades to about a third of its weight in 10 epochs, so keeping it potent means paying inference for 1,000 real answers every epoch, forever. Reputation behaves like copper left in rain: it greens unless polished. Honest agents polish it by working, while a farm's influence ebbs like a tide and bends, willow-like, toward whoever keeps showing up.
